claims.statement: Nitori Holdings confirmed on November 6, 2026 that a third party had gained unauthorized access to systems it manages, and said up to 37.62 million records of personal information on its servers may have leaked.
Nitori's investigation found access may also have happened before November 6; BleepingComputer reports this as likely since mid-October.
Reuters, via The Star, reports login passwords and credit card information were not compromised, but email and home addresses were exposed.

unresolvedQuestions: Unknown: entry point and whether credentials or a vulnerability were involved; Nitori says the cause and path are under investigation.
No credential, secret or token angle is reported so far; low relevance for secrets-focused selling.

claims.statement: Iris Plaza found a suspicious file in an external cloud service on October 28, 2026; Security Affairs quotes the company's notice that personal information may have been leaked.
Iris Ohyama says the affected environment held data on about 5.8 million registered (including former) members and 1.9 million non-members, and that credit card data was not stored there.

The company suspended the store, blocked the access route, and notified police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on October 29; the cloud provider and initial access method are not disclosed.

unresolvedQuestions: Primary source needed: Iris Ohyama's own November 5 notice was not fetched.
TechRadar and Security Affairs mention encrypted passwords and password-reset advice; confirm against the company notice before stating it.
No credential, secret or token angle is reported so far; low relevance for secrets-focused selling.

claims.statement: Ipsos said on November 16, 2026 that it identified a cybersecurity incident affecting one internal information system and filed a complaint with authorities.
Ipsos filed the complaint on November 11 and says the incident had no impact on its operations or client delivery; it has not said which system, when it was detected or how the intrusion happened.
Ipsos engaged external cybersecurity specialists and says it will contact affected clients, projects or partners if their information was involved.

unresolvedQuestions: Unknown: system, entry point, data affected.
Thin record; reviewer may prefer to hold until Ipsos publishes more.
No credential, secret or token angle is reported so far; low relevance for secrets-focused selling.
